text.p: Industrial metals prices stabilised overnight after a sharp reverse in copper but it was gold's turn to be hit as speculators baled out in favour of a prospect of better returns in the bond market.
Gold fixed in London at $379.70 per ounce compared with $381.70 on Tuesday afternoon.
Wheat prices were 4-1/2 cents lower to one cent higher per bushel while oil prices eased.
The CRB index was up 0.58 points at 241.69.

Copper prices leapt higher with the market doing a 180-degree turn and finishing close to the peaks of the day's $55 range. Traders said an impressive recovery from a midday low of $1,900 was mostly due to shortcovering after earlier speculative selling failed to hit the sub-$1,900 stops. But widening spreads, notably due to tight nearbys, also restored some calm after Tuesday's savage declines.

But despite the smooth recovery from the midsession slump, copper's general trend remains unclear. Given that stocks are at their lowest for six years, with no metal being delivered into warehouses at all, prices should be nearer $2,300, some said.

"Copper is carrying a lot of baggage around at the moment. There could be some Sumitomo positions still around, we've got options (November declarations) coming up next week, and the Chinese are either buying or selling, depending on who you talk to," another trader said.
Accordingly, short-term trading will remain muddied by uncertainty, with big-volume, large price-swing days on the horizon. "I would not like to call the next $100 move,", an analyst said.

Elsewhere in a lively metals complex aluminium tended to mirror copper throughout the session, easing back to near the $1,400 level, then recovering against a backdrop of some trade buying. Prices finished at $1,428, up $21 from Tuesday.
Nickel spurted higher as well, bouyed by the trend in copper and against a background of talk of possible disruption in New Caledonia, although details were scarce.
Prices pivoted around the $7,300 level at one stage before uncovering some support and chasing up to end the kerb at $7,340 a tonne, against Tuesday's close of $7,325.
The zinc market was heartened by recent upmoves and fund buying. Prices flipped above the $1,050 level in fairly lively late trading to close the day at $1,053, up $11.
Lead moved higher in undramatic trading, but appears to be underpinned by expectations of reasonable battery demand this
Gold closed in London at $379.80/$380.30 vs $381.25/$381.75 previously and was flirting with key $380.00 support.

Downside targets were seen at $379 and $376.90 after the metal was hit by fund selling early in New York where it was quoted at $380.00/380.50 in late trading. Comex gold closed 30 cents lower at $381.30 for December delivery.
"We're getting to critical levels," a London-based dealer said. "If the pressure stays on gold it'll head down to $375..."
Talk that European central banks may sell gold as European Union countries seek to meet the 1999 single currency criteria has been depressing sentiment, dealers said.

Crude oil futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange were lower across the board on Wednesday, pulled down mainly by heating oil futures which sunk after another weekly build in stocks, traders said.

Though the American Petroleum Institute and the Energy Department reported declines in crude and gasoline stocks, market participants were focusing on the build of more than five million barrels in distillate stocks in the key PADD I (northeast) U.S. district over the past two weeks.
December WTI crude was quoted at $24.25 a barrel around the close, down 10 cents.

WHEAT - Wheat closed mostly lower in quiet trading with the market underpinned by signals that it was oversold in the near term. Fundmentals were little changed. December was 3-1/2 cents lower at 381 cents a bushel.
